15import logging 

16 

17import torch 

18 

19logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

20 

21# Resolved once at import time (dense_dim.py / _dimI.py precedent): the 

22# per-call ``torch.sparse_coo`` attribute walk is removable host slack, and 

23# layout enum members are singletons, so ``is`` is equivalent to ``==``. 

24_SPARSE_COO = torch.sparse_coo 

25 

26 

27def _dimV(self: torch.Tensor) -> int: 

28 """Return the number of dense dimensions of a sparse COO tensor ``self``. 

29 

30 Mirrors ``aten::_dimV(Tensor self) -> int``. This is a pure layout-metadata 

31 query: the result never depends on stored element data, so it is computed 

32 from TensorImpl properties without re-dispatching the ``_dimV`` operator 

33 itself (re-entering the dispatcher from inside a registered Sparse kernel 

34 would recurse into this implementation). 

35 

36 Semantics by layout (verified against native ATen on H20, torch 

37 2.8.0a0+5228986c39.nv25.05): 

38 - ``torch.sparse_coo``: ``sparse_dim`` equals ``self._indices().shape[0]`` 

39 (the leading index-matrix dimension), so ``_dimV == dim() - 

40 indices.shape[0]``. Plain 2-D COO gives 0, hybrid COO tensors (values 

41 with trailing dense dimensions) give ``dim() - 1``, zero-nnz and 

42 uncoalesced COO behave identically to coalesced plain COO (metadata is 

43 unaffected by coalescing state). 

44 - Every other layout: native ATen registers ``aten::_dimV`` only for the 

45 Sparse (COO) backends — strided, CSR/CSC (and BSR/BSC) raise 

46 ``NotImplementedError`` natively ("Could not run 'aten::_dimV' ... from 

47 the 'CUDA'/'SparseCsrCUDA' backend"). Mirror that contract here instead 

48 of guessing a formula. 

49 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME _DIMV") 

50 

51 Enflame-local hot-path deviation (gcu400 copy): the operator has no 

52 device kernel (GCU400 has no sparse-COO TensorImpl; benchmark/test_dimV 

53 inputs are CPU-resident COO built through the shared construction 

54 fallback), so its whole cost is host-side Python. Interleaved timeit 

55 (GCU400, torch 2.11, 5 rounds x 30x2000) puts the previous body at 

56 ~574ns per direct call, dominated by ``self._indices().shape[0]`` 

57 (~470ns: one dispatcher round-trip plus a fresh tensor-object wrap per 

58 call; ``self.sparse_dim()`` is worse at ~1.58us). The COO value is 

59 instead read via ``self.dense_dim()`` (~258ns, one dispatcher 

60 round-trip returning a plain int) — the registered FlagGems sibling 

61 metadata op that shares the exact COO semantics (FlagGems op 

62 composition per the host-function contract; no recursion: the dense_dim 

63 implementation never re-enters ``_dimV``), while this wrapper keeps the 

64 ``_dimV``-only layout contract (non-COO raises; dense_dim alone would 

65 answer 0 for compressed layouts). With the layout constant resolved at 

66 import time and the singleton ``is`` compare, the direct call measures 

67 ~322ns (-44%). Note that the official KERNEL-mode harness floors at 

68 ~2.1us for any host-only call (an empty lambda measures the same), so 

69 this gain is visible only in wall-clock timeit, not in the event-based 

70 kernel-mode record (dense_dim.py / _unsafe_view.py precedent). 

71 """ 

72 if self.layout is _SPARSE_COO: 

73 return self.dense_dim() 

74 raise NotImplementedError( 

75 f"Could not run 'aten::_dimV' with arguments from the '{self.layout}' layout; " 

76 "aten::_dimV is only registered for the Sparse (COO) backends" 

77 )
